ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a boost-type DC-DC converter. The DC input source on the left is labeled Vi = 20 V; after the input, an inductor is connected in series, labeled L = 2 mH, and the inductor current is ii; the node at the right end of the inductor is connected to the bottom common reference line through a switch S; the same node is connected through a diode to the output terminal on the right; the output terminal has a capacitor and a load resistor connected in parallel, the output voltage is labeled V0 = 40 V, the load resistor is labeled 10 Ω, and the output current is i0. Therefore this is a boost converter with a grounded-reference switch. Reasoning calculation: The switching frequency is known as fs = 500 Hz, so the switching period Ts = 1/fs = 1/500 = 0.002 s = 2 ms. In continuous conduction mode, an ideal boost converter satisfies V0 = Vi/(1-D). Substituting 40 = 20/(1-D), obtain 1-D = 0.5, so D = 0.5, and the on-time ton = D Ts = 0.5 × 2 ms = 1 ms. The load power Pout = V0^2/R = 40^2/10 = 160 W. In the ideal case, the input power equals the output power, so the average input current is also the average inductor current IL,avg = Pin/Vi = 160/20 = 8 A. During the switch on-time, the voltage across the inductor is Vi = 20 V, therefore the peak-to-peak value of the inductor current ripple ΔIL = (Vi/L) ton = (20/0.002) × 0.001 = 10 A. The inductor current is a triangular wave, so the peak inductor current IL,peak = IL,avg + ΔIL/2 = 8 + 10/2 = 13 A.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the switch shorts the inductor right terminal to ground during on-time, and during off-time the inductor current flows through the diode into the output capacitor/load. From the text, use f_s=500 Hz, so T_s=2 ms, and take V0=40 V constant. In the on-state, v_L=20 V, so the current rises with slope 20/2 mH. Final answer: 13 A

In the ideal case, the input power equals the output power, so the average input current is also the average inductor current IL,avg = Pin/Vi = 160/20 = 8 A. During the switch on-time, the voltage across the inductor is Vi = 20 V, therefore the peak-to-peak value of the inductor current ripple ΔIL = (Vi/L) ton = (20/0.002) × 0.001 = 10 A. The inductor current is a triangular wave, so the peak inductor current IL,peak = IL,avg + ΔIL/2 = 8 + 10/2 = 13 A.
